title: Brad’s Kale Chips Recalled Nationwide Over Thallium Contamination
excerpt: Snack Right Super Foods is recalling Brad’s Plant Based Crunchy Kale and Veggie Chips Kale products, about 25,000 bags, because they may contain thallium.
content:
Snack Right Super Foods Inc., doing business as Brad’s Raw Chips, is recalling Brad’s Plant Based Crunchy Kale and Brad’s Veggie Chips Kale products because they may contain thallium, Food Safety News reported November 3.

Thallium is a naturally occurring metal found in soil and in sulfur-based minerals. It can be taken up by plants and vegetables, particularly those in the Brassica family, including kale, cabbage and radish. Acute or chronic exposure to thallium can result in serious adverse health effects, including gastroenteritis, damage to peripheral nerves and hair loss, according to the report.

The products were distributed nationwide through KeHE Distributors and United Natural Foods Inc. (UNFI), and sold directly to five individual consumers. Approximately 25,000 bags are estimated to be in commerce, with distribution between October 2025 and December 2025.

The recall covers Brad’s Crunchy Kale, Original, 2-ounce bags (UPC 813104021679); Brad’s Crunchy Kale, Cheeze It Up, 2-ounce bags (UPC 813104021877); Brad’s Crunchy Kale, Radical Ranch, 2-ounce bags (UPC 813104020726); and Brad’s Veggie Chips Kale, 3-ounce bags (UPC 854615002054), with the specific lot numbers and best-by dates listed in the recall notice. Shoppers should check the lot number and best-by date on the bag against the recall list.

The backstory matters: in May 2026, the California Department of Public Health advised consumers not to eat certain Brad’s Plant Based products after investigating an inquiry from one individual with elevated thallium levels. The department collected samples at retail stores in the Sacramento area, and laboratory testing found elevated thallium levels in multiple varieties. The recall was initiated after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration advised the firm of thallium in tested products.

The report notes that the manufacturing process did not introduce the contaminant, but the dehydration process removes about 85 to 90 percent of the product’s water, which concentrates elements already present in the fresh kale.

What to do

Consumers who purchased any of the listed products should stop consuming them immediately and discard the product, according to the recall notice. Refunds are not being offered, and the product should not be returned to the place of purchase.

Sources:

  • Food Safety News, “Kale chips recalled because of thallium contamination” (Nov. 3, 2026)
